cf.title: Require SSL connection to postgres for oauth

input.subject: Require SSL connection to postgres for oauth

verdict_reasoning: The goal has support in the thread, and the doc patch 0001 raises no objection. The client-side check in 0002 fails at level 2: already-exists-1 and standards-compat-1 show an OAuth-only transport rule whose only opt-out is a debug flag, against setups message #6 calls common. security-1 and standards-compat-2 are open design points on 0002 and 0003. The list has to agree on the policy scope and the opt-out before code review of 0002 makes sense.

brief.title: Require encrypted connections for OAuth bearer tokens in libpq
brief.problem: libpq sends the OAuth bearer token to the server over plaintext TCP without warning, though RFC 7628 says TLS MUST protect it. Clients can leak a token by accident, and the docs warn about clear-text passwords but say nothing about OAuth.
brief.proposed_design: Three patches. 0001 adds doc warnings that OAuth over unencrypted connections exposes the token. 0002 makes libpq refuse the OAUTHBEARER exchange unless the connection uses SSL/TLS, GSSAPI encryption or a Unix-domain socket, with an unsafe debug flag to restore the old behavior. 0003 makes the server warn when an oauth HBA entry allows plaintext connections.
user_visible_surface: libpq refuses OAUTHBEARER over unencrypted TCP connections by default (0002).
New PGOAUTHDEBUG option UNSAFE:plaintext-server; the legacy PGOAUTHDEBUG=UNSAFE enables it implicitly.
Server WARNING from HBA parsing for oauth entries of type host, hostnossl or hostnogss, at start, reload and in pg_hba_file_rules() (0003).
New warnings about plaintext OAuth in client-auth.sgml and protocol.sgml (0001).
author_claims: RFC 7628 and RFC 6750 require TLS to protect bearer tokens, unlike SCRAM, which only recommends it.
The libpq default is inconsistent: HTTPS to the identity provider needs an unsafe flag to bypass, the server connection does not.
Unix-domain sockets are local and so a safe exception.
0003 improves safety without breaking any use case.
The doc patch alone, or with the server warning, helps all supported versions.
brief.thread_state: Jacob Champion and Jonathan Gonzalez raised compatibility concerns about non-TLS setups in Kubernetes and tunnels, and Daniel Gustafsson plans to commit a reworked doc patch for master through 18. The client-side change is deferred to v20 at the earliest, and the server warning has no review yet.
unclear: Whether the server warning should also cover password and ident entries, as the author asked.
How the client check treats sslmode=prefer or allow when the connection falls back to plaintext.
Whether file-based libpq configuration would replace the PGOAUTHDEBUG opt-out flag.
What the HBA warning says, and whether it fires for hostssl entries combined with other settings.
Whether the CF entry still tracks 0002, which reviewers saw as not ready.

objections.title: 0002 breaks working plaintext OAuth setups, and the only opt-out is a debug flag
objections.failure_scenario: A team reaches Postgres through kubectl port-forward or a service-mesh tunnel without TLS. After a distribution upgrades libpq, every OAuth login fails, even though the server did not change. The only fix is setting PGOAUTHDEBUG=UNSAFE:plaintext-server in production, which the docs describe as a debug option for local testing.
objections.argument: Message #6 reports that plaintext OAuth over Kubernetes and cloud port-forwards is common and sometimes required, because TLS through those tunnels gets reset. Message #4 objects that a transport default for one authentication type makes users track per-method rules, and asks for one policy for all methods. Message #7 defers the change to v20, but the opt-out design is still the debug flag. The author's other ideas, an explicit sslmode=disable or the file-based configuration from message #2, are not part of the patch.
objections.author_must_show: What supported, non-debug setting will a production user in a non-TLS tunnel use, and how does it fit a policy that later covers SCRAM and password too?

critic.reasoning: Message #6 describes non-TLS tunnels as common, and the 0002 commit message limits the opt-out to "local development and testing". Message #2 doubts these users should need a debug flag, and no later patch version changes that.

objections.title: OAuth-only transport check duplicates sslmode and require_auth
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA hardens a cluster on the assumption that libpq now refuses plaintext for credentials. SCRAM and password connections from the same client still go over plaintext TCP, because only OAUTHBEARER has the new check. A user with a tunnel setup has to move between sslmode, require_auth and a PGOAUTHDEBUG flag to get either the old behavior or a strict one.
objections.argument: Clients can already refuse plaintext with sslmode=require or verify-full, combined with require_auth=oauth, and servers can already enforce it with hostssl entries. 0002 adds a second, OAuth-only way to get the same result, and its opt-out is a debug flag. In message #4 Jacob argues that per-mechanism transport defaults are "probably not a net win". In message #2 he names file-based libpq configuration as the general place for a stricter default. The author's answer, that the RFC requires TLS for OAUTHBEARER, explains why the default should change but not why the change should be OAuth-only.
objections.author_must_show: Why should OAuth get its own transport check instead of a stricter default in sslmode or require_auth that covers every authentication method?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 argues that per-method transport defaults are probably not a net win, and the thread does not answer that. The RFC argument explains a stricter default but does not explain why only OAUTHBEARER gets it.

objections.title: Client check accepts TLS without server certificate verification
objections.failure_scenario: A user connects with sslmode=require, as the proposed error message would suggest. An active attacker on the path presents its own certificate, libpq accepts it because the connection is encrypted, and the bearer token is sent to the attacker. The attacker can replay the token against the real server, and nobody notices.
objections.argument: The 0002 commit message cites RFC 6750 Sec. 5 but accepts any SSL/TLS connection, and the RFC protection assumes the client verifies the server certificate. OAUTHBEARER has no channel binding (protocol.sgml), so an unauthenticated TLS peer can capture a token and replay it. Message #3 proposes an error hint of "consider sslmode=require", which points users to a mode that does not authenticate the server. Message #4 notes that sslmode defaults are the real gap. A check that blocks passive sniffing but lets an active MITM through may give users more confidence than the design supports.
objections.author_must_show: Will the check and its error message require or recommend sslmode=verify-full or sslrootcert=system, and if not, why is unauthenticated TLS enough for a replayable token?

critic.reasoning: 0002 accepts any SSL/TLS connection, and sslmode=require does not verify the server certificate. The patch does not make this worse than today, but it cites the RFCs as its basis, so the level of protection it requires is a fair design question.

objections.title: 0003 warns about oauth HBA lines only, with no way to silence it
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA whose clients all set sslmode=require keeps a plain host oauth line. The DBA gets a WARNING at every start and reload, and monitoring that queries pg_hba_file_rules() gets one too. A host password line on the same server produces no warning, which suggests that password over plaintext is safer than OAuth.
objections.argument: The patch adds warnings for oauth only, and the author's question in message #5 about extending them to password and ident got no answer. pg_hba_file_rules() reports problems in its error column, so a WARNING raised during a SELECT works differently from that. Users whose plaintext setup is intended, as in message #6, have no setting to turn the warning off. The claim in message #8 that 0003 breaks no use case does not cover log noise or what tools see.
objections.author_must_show: Why should only oauth entries warn, and how does a DBA with an intended plaintext setup stop the warning on every reload?

critic.reasoning: A DBA whose clients all use TLS can switch to hostssl, but an intended plaintext setup has no way to silence the warning. The oauth-only scope and the WARNING raised from pg_hba_file_rules() are open; message #5's question got no answer.

refuted.title: Client-side OAuth-only TLS rule repeats a design choice made on purpose
refuted.failure_scenario: A team connects through a kubectl port-forward or mesh tunnel with sslmode=prefer. After an upgrade, SCRAM logins keep working but OAuth logins fail in libpq, and only the debug variable PGOAUTHDEBUG=UNSAFE:plaintext-server restores them. They first see this as a broken login.
refuted.argument: Message #2 reports that in-person discussions of this enforcement drew a neutral-to-negative reaction. Message #4 says the plaintext behaviour was an explicit decision, and that a separate transport-security default per auth type is probably not a net win. The author points to RFC 7628's MUST, but message #4 replies that the Postgres security model covers every method, and message #6 describes common setups without TLS.
refuted.author_must_show: Why should libpq enforce transport encryption for OAUTHBEARER alone, instead of waiting for a stricter default that covers all secrets, as message #4 proposes?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of already-exists-1. The prior-rejection framing is also weak: message #2 says "I wouldn't mind enforcing this if there's consensus", and message #7 hopes to raise the bar in v20.

refuted.title: OAuth-only transport rule pushes production users onto a debug flag
refuted.failure_scenario: A Kubernetes team uses port-forward without TLS, as message #6 describes, and their OAuth logins start failing after the upgrade. They set PGOAUTHDEBUG=UNSAFE in production images to get them working again. The legacy form also turns on every other unsafe option, including plaintext HTTP to the identity provider, so the team exposes more than the one setting they needed.
refuted.argument: In message #4 Jacob Champion argues against different transport defaults for different authentication types, and he prefers a policy for all secrets through file-based libpq configuration. Patch 0002 adds an OAuth-only rule, and its only opt-out is a flag documented for local development and testing. If file-based configuration lands later, the project keeps two opt-outs for the same policy. Message #6 shows that non-TLS deployments are common, so this flag would become routine production configuration.
refuted.author_must_show: What supported, non-debug setting should users with a required non-TLS path use, and how would it fold into a later policy covering all authentication methods?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. The point about legacy PGOAUTHDEBUG=UNSAFE enabling the other unsafe options is a useful detail, but it supports the same objection about the debug-flag opt-out.

refuted.title: HBA warning fires on ordinary host entries and cannot be silenced
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA uses "host ... oauth" entries, and every client connects with sslmode=require. The server still logs a WARNING at every start and reload, and the same warning appears in pg_hba_file_rules(). Once the warning is also extended to password and ident entries, as message #5 proposes, most installations warn on every reload, and DBAs learn to ignore it.
refuted.argument: Patch 0003 warns on the connection type of the entry, which says nothing about whether clients actually use TLS. The proposal offers no way for a DBA who has accepted the risk to silence the warning, for example in the cases from message #6. A warning that fires in correct setups adds log noise for everyone. The extension proposed in message #5 would multiply that noise across authentication methods.
refuted.author_must_show: How does a DBA whose clients always use TLS, or who has accepted a non-TLS path, avoid a warning at every reload?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2. The added scenario depends on an extension to password and ident that message #5 only asks about and no patch contains.

refuted.title: Client-side refusal rests on one in-house report, with a workaround available
refuted.failure_scenario: A team runs OAuth over plaintext TCP inside a service mesh or a kubectl port-forward tunnel. After upgrading libpq to v20, every connection fails at the OAUTHBEARER step. The team then has to set an option the docs label as an unsafe debug flag in production.
refuted.argument: The only demand in the material is one report from the author's own company (the Reported-by line in the first 0001). No field report or -general thread shows users leaking tokens by accident. Message #6 says the opposite group, plaintext OAuth in Kubernetes and cloud tunnels, is common. Users who want protection already have it today: `hostssl` in the HBA plus `sslmode=require` and `require_auth` on the client (message #4).
refuted.author_must_show: Which users have sent bearer tokens over plaintext by accident, and why do `hostssl` plus `sslmode=require` not already protect them?

critic.reasoning: Two committers who know the area say they want stricter transport defaults (messages #4 and #7), so interest goes beyond one report. hostssl and sslmode=require do not protect a client user who is unaware of the risk, and the breakage scenario duplicates standards-compat-1.

refuted.title: OAuth-only HBA warning lands on intentional plaintext setups
refuted.failure_scenario: A Kubernetes operator uses `host ... oauth` on purpose, behind a mesh. 0003 then emits a WARNING at every start and reload, and on every pg_hba_file_rules() query. The proposal gives no way to silence the warning for this deliberate configuration.
refuted.argument: 0003 targets the group that message #6 calls common and deliberate, while the benefit goes to DBAs who misconfigured by accident, and no such case is shown. Message #4 asks for one transport-security policy across all auth methods, and message #5 asks whether password and ident should be covered too. Without an answer, the OAuth-only warning may need to be redone later.
refuted.author_must_show: How would an operator who runs OAuth over plaintext on purpose avoid a recurring WARNING, and why warn for oauth entries but not password entries?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2. Message #2 also supports a server-side warning regardless of the client change, which weakens the desirability framing.

touch_points.label: wire protocol
touch_points.reason: libpq refuses the OAUTHBEARER SASL exchange on unencrypted TCP; no message format changes.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: see objection standards-compat-1: 0002 breaks working plaintext OAuth setups, and the only opt-out is a debug flag

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: Every libpq client, psql included, gets a new connection failure for OAuth over plaintext TCP.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: 0002 changes when libpq sends a bearer token; 0003 warns about oauth HBA entries that allow plaintext.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The author wanted the fix in earlier branches; 0002 changes default behavior, so only the doc patch is planned for 18.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: A new PGOAUTHDEBUG option and an OAuth-only transport rule may overlap with later file-based libpq configuration.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: sslmode, require_auth and hostssl entries already let clients and servers refuse plaintext OAuth.

questions: What supported, non-debug setting will a production user on a non-TLS tunnel use to keep OAuth working after 0002?
Why should libpq enforce encryption for OAUTHBEARER alone, instead of a stricter default that covers SCRAM and password too?
Does the client check accept sslmode=require without server certificate verification, and if so, why is that enough for a replayable token?
How does 0002 treat sslmode=prefer or allow when the connection falls back to plaintext?
Why does 0003 warn only for oauth entries, and how does a DBA with an intended plaintext setup silence it?

committability.owner_note: Jacob Champion and Daniel Gustafsson take part in the thread; the brief says Daniel Gustafsson plans to commit a reworked doc patch. 0002 and 0003 need someone who knows libpq authentication and HBA parsing.
committability.liability: For 0002, a default behavior change in libpq that breaks existing non-TLS OAuth setups, plus a PGOAUTHDEBUG option that must stay supported once production users depend on it. For 0003, a recurring server WARNING that users will ask to silence.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 and v3 in response to review and moved the entry to a later CommitFest; the entry has needed a rebase since 2026-11-07.

priority.reason: The patches are small and touch only libpq OAuth code, hba.c and docs, but 0002 changes a default for OAuth users and its opt-out is a debug flag. The doc patch can proceed alone; 0002 and 0003 need agreement on policy scope and opt-out first.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the behavior under sslmode=prefer fallback, the exact warning text, and how pg_hba_file_rules() reports the warning could not be checked. Only 3 of 9 messages were visible; later messages are known through the objections and the brief.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Missing dependency on oauth_validator test
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the `oauth_hook_client` binary as a test dependency in the oauth_validator meson.build file, so the binary is built before the test runs. Without it, `meson test --suite oauth_validator` failed when the build did not enable the OAuth test through `PG_EXTRA_TEST`.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The only message is the author's proposal, and there are no replies.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add sslmode "no-clientcert" to avoid auth failure in md5/scram connections
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a new libpq sslmode value, "no-clientcert", that makes libpq ignore the default client certificate and key in ~/.postgresql/. A user with those files could then still connect with password authentication to servers that do not know the certificate.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch because Jacob Champion's separate patchset adds sslcertmode=disable, which already stops libpq from sending a client certificate. Reviewers found that option the more elegant way to get the same result. Jelte Fennema also pointed out that setting sslcert to a file that does not exist already works around the problem.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm withdrawing this patch, as the same feature was already implemented
in a different patch written by Jacob[1]

precedents_retrieved.title: OAuth Followup Patches
precedents_retrieved.summary: Follow-up patches to the OAUTHBEARER SASL authentication support in libpq and the server, which uses the OAuth Device Authorization flow through libcurl. The visible work moves the libcurl-based flow into a separate libpq-oauth module loaded by dlopen() and fixes build and packaging problems on several platforms.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The libpq-oauth module split and its build fixes were committed in May 2025, and the author said he would move a remaining libcurl file-descriptor bug on BSD to its own thread.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve OAuth discovery logging [accidental duplicate]
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch stops the server from logging a FATAL OAuth bearer authentication failure when a client sends an empty token to discover the issuer URL. It adds a new SASL exchange status, PG_SASL_EXCHANGE_ABANDONED (first named PG_SASL_EXCHANGE_RESTART), which auth-sasl.c maps to STATUS_EOF.
precedents_retrieved.objection: This commitfest entry was a duplicate of entry 6529, which Jacob Champion created by mistake and then withdrew. The patch itself was not rejected, and he said the other entry was in his commit queue.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
(I didn't read adequately and ended up duplicating the patch in CF;
I've withdrawn that.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_hba_lookup function to get all matching pg_hba.conf entries
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a SQL function pg_hba_lookup that takes a database, a user and optionally an address and hostname, and returns the pg_hba.conf entries that match them, in match order. It replaces an earlier attempt at a catalog view of pg_hba.conf, which could not handle keywords in the database and user columns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: At the end of the last commitfest for 9.6, Tom Lane reviewed the patch and judged it not ready to commit. He found the patch too invasive in the authentication code, raised concerns about its memory management and its function signature, and found type errors in the docs. He also doubted the use case, since a user who cannot connect cannot run the function, and suggested making log_connections record the matched pg_hba line.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
And it's not very clear that it'll help
with "I can't connect", either, because if you can't connect you're
not going to be running this function.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add inline comments to the pg_hba_file_rules view
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Daniel Gustafsson, Greg Sabino Mullane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a "comment" column to the pg_hba_file_rules view that shows the end-of-line comment of each valid pg_hba.conf entry. The author wanted this so annotations such as tags or client names on hba entries can be read through SQL.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut objected that end-of-line comments are only one of several comment styles, so showing only them is incomplete, and that users may not want file comments exposed through a view. Daniel Gustafsson and Greg Sabino Mullane agreed. Daniel proposed agreeing on a separate annotation syntax for pg_hba.conf in a new thread, and the author withdrew the patch to start that discussion.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think we should leave file comments be file comments.  If we want some annotations to be exported to higher-level views, we should make that an intentional and explicit separate feature.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_hba_file_settings
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a system view, first named pg_hba_file_settings and later pg_hba_rules, that shows each line of pg_hba.conf with any parse error, similar to pg_file_settings. It lets users check pg_hba.conf before a reload and shows each rule's options in a jsonb column, built with new helper functions such as push_jsonb_string_value().
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier moved it to the next CF with no reviews, then marked it returned with feedback. He questioned the use of jsonb for the options column, since the options are not nested and a simple name=value array would do. Vitaly Burovoy argued for jsonb to make filtering easier, but the thread ended without a revised patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If they were nested I'd see a case for it but it
seems to me that as presented this is just an overkill. In short, I
think that this patch needs a bit of rework, so I am marking it as
returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix warnings under ENFORCE_REGRESSION_TEST_NAME_RESTRICTIONS
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch renamed roles and databases in the SSL TAP tests to use the regress_ and regression_ prefixes, and regenerated the certificates to match. This removed the backend warnings that the SSL tests produce when Postgres is built with ENFORCE_REGRESSION_TEST_NAME_RESTRICTIONS.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The naming rule exists to protect clusters with useful data during "make installcheck", and TAP tests always run on one-off clusters, so they have nothing to protect. Extending the rule to TAP tests would need the WARNING raised to an ERROR to find all violations, and fixing a single TAP suite was judged not worth doing. About 400 similar warnings remained after the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
TAP tests always use one-off test clusters, so there is no hazard
to guard against.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 7c1849311e49, due to the fact that more than 60% of
the buildfarm members do not have lz4 installed.  As we are in the last
commit fest of the development cycle, and that it could take a couple
of weeks to stabilize things, this change is reverted for now.

This commit will be reworked in a lighter version, as
default_toast_compression's default can be changed to "lz4" without the
switch from --with-lz4 to --without-lz4.  This approach will keep the
buildfarm at bay, and still allow builds to take advantage of LZ4 in

A harder requirement based on LZ4 should be achievable at some point,
but it is going to require some work from the buildfarm owners first.
Perhaps this part could be revisited at the beginning of the next
development cycle.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return historic snapshot during LR
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return historic snapshot during LR
Reverted commit(s): Don't allow GetTransactionSnapshot() in logical decoding
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 1585ff7387 changed GetTransactionSnapshot() to throw an error
if it's called during logical decoding, instead of returning the
historic snapshot. I made that change for extra protection, because a
historic snapshot can only be used to access catalog tables while
GetTransactionSnapshot() is usually called when you're executing
arbitrary queries. You might get very subtle visibility problems if
you tried to use the historic snapshot for arbitrary queries.

There's no built-in code in PostgreSQL that calls
GetTransactionSnapshot() during logical decoding, but it turns out
that the pglogical extension does just that, to evaluate row filter
expressions. You would get weird results if the row filter runs
arbitrary queries, but it is sane as long as you don't access any
non-catalog tables. Even though there are no checks to enforce that in
pglogical, a typical row filter expression does not access any tables
and works fine. Accessing tables marked with the user_catalog_table =
true option is also OK.

To fix pglogical with row filters, and any other extensions that might
do similar things, revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return a
historic snapshot during logical decoding.

To try to still catch the unsafe usage of historic snapshots, add
checks in heap_beginscan() and index_beginscan() to complain if you
try to use a historic snapshot to scan a non-catalog table. We're very
close to the version 18 release however, so add those new checks only
in master.

roaster_notes.note: [P23] proposed a warning about unencrypted passwords and was withdrawn with no recorded reason, so it is not listed as a prior attempt. The doc patch 0001 is moving toward commit, and the server warning 0003 has no recorded earlier objection.
The 0001 doc warnings raise no standards or compatibility concern, and a committer plans to apply them.

The proposal changes no persistent or replicated state: no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire message or extension ABI. The client check and the HBA warning act at authentication time only, and messages #2, #6 and #7 already raised the tunnel and pooler compatibility concern that led to deferring 0002.
The proposal hardens security, and the server warning in 0003 exposes nothing new to unprivileged users. The one gap is that encrypted is treated as safe even when the server is not authenticated.
No objection to the doc patch 0001, which a committer has reworked and plans to commit.
0001 (docs) and 0003 (HBA warning) do not duplicate an existing mechanism, so this angle raises nothing against them.

The doc patch (0001) has committer support and real value, so there is no demand objection to it. [P23] proposed a similar password warning and was withdrawn, but its reason is not recorded, so it is not cited.
